data.content_ref: inline:The problem standard fixes straight cuts through the exact center, which under the standard mathematical idealization (zero-width lines, single center point) yields a finite, well-defined count; the target's claim of 'unbounded or undefined' relies on explicitly excluded counterconditions (non-zero thickness or distinct-but-near intersection points). It concedes that for ideal mathematical lines 'this is not the case,' yet retains the unbounded/undefined claim, contradicting the problem's stated idealization.
